flags.finding: [partially supported] The screenplay uses the name "The Glades Motel" as a specific location in scene S048. flags.finding: [partially supported] The brand name "FDS" (feminine hygiene spray) is mentioned in dialogue in scene S064, and the context implies it is used as a weapon, causing discomfort ("stings"). This could be interpreted as a negative depiction or disparagement of the brand, potentially leading to a demand letter from the trademark owner (Alberto-Culver Company). While such use is often defensible under expressive-work protections, it carries litigation risk.

Consider softening the depiction of harm, or replacing the product name with a fictional one. Adding a disclaimer that the product's depiction is fictional and not intended to reflect its actual properties could also mitigate risk. The cost would primarily be for legal defense, not damages, as the use is likely defensible.

flags.finding: [partially supported] Scene S064 depicts a character being shot and killed. This involves the use of a firearm and special effects to simulate a fatal injury. The use of firearms, even with blanks, is inherently dangerous and requires highly specialized personnel and strict safety protocols to prevent serious injury or death to cast and crew. The script describes Dante's "chest exploding," which implies the use of squibs or other pyrotechnic effects.

citations.title: Bullet hit squib - Wikipedia
citations.excerpt: The production company is responsible for ensuring safety when using firearms, explosives, and squibs on film sets. Special permits to notify local authorities are needed for squib use—specifying the number of takes, number of squibs per take, types of squibs and distance from talent.

citations.title: We are filmmakers who work with firearms. This is what is important in on-set safety
citations.excerpt: A gun with no ammunition – that is, a gun with neither a bullet nor blanks – is not dangerous. But even so, on set there is always an armourer, a safety officer, and a stunt coordinator: at least three people who always have an eye on the guns on set.

citations.title: Violence & Weapons Safety for Films - InFocus Film School
citations.excerpt: Because they only have a small, electronically triggered squib in the barrel and don’t require blanks, non-guns are significantly safer and quieter than guns.

remedy.detail: A qualified armourer/weapons specialist, a stunt coordinator, and a special effects coordinator are mandatory for this scene. The production must obtain all necessary permits for firearm and squib use. Strong consideration should be given to using non-guns with VFX for muzzle flash and bullet impacts, or entirely VFX-generated gunshot effects, to minimize on-set risk. If blanks are used, strict adherence to industry safety standards, including test firing and clear safety zones, is paramount.

flags.finding: Scene S019 depicts Veronica discharging a fire extinguisher at a crowd and an individual in an enclosed convenience store. The chemical discharge from a fire extinguisher can cause respiratory, skin, and eye irritation, and in poorly ventilated areas, can lead to more serious toxicity.

citations.title: Fire extinguisher safety | Poison Control
citations.excerpt: Fire extinguishers, when used properly, are generally safe. However, there is some risk for mild respiratory, skin, or eye irritation. The use of a fire extinguisher in areas with poor air flow, or intentional inhalation of fire extinguishers, can produce serious toxicity that would require medical evaluation.

citations.title: Fire extinguisher safety | Poison Control
citations.excerpt: Air out any area where a fire extinguisher has been discharged before reentering it.

remedy.detail: Replace the real fire extinguisher with a theatrical prop that discharges a non-toxic, non-irritating substance (e.g., cornstarch or a similar inert powder). Ensure adequate ventilation in the set during and after discharge. Performers being sprayed should be informed and provided with eye protection if necessary. A safety supervisor should be present to oversee the safe execution of the effect.

flags.finding: The script features a dog in scenes S001, S002, S005 and a cat in scenes S009, S025, S029, S038, S047, S053, S055. The presence of live animals on set necessitates the engagement of qualified animal handlers and strict adherence to animal welfare protocols to ensure their safety and well-being, as well as the safety of the cast and crew.

citations.title: General Guidelines for Filmed Media - American Humane Society
citations.excerpt: Production should only use animal handlers who are knowledgeable about the species of animal to be used and familiar with set protocol.

citations.title: General Guidelines for Filmed Media - American Humane Society
citations.excerpt: Adequate exercise and rest, as determined or agreed to by the American Humane Certified Animal Safety Representative, shall be provided for the animals during the shooting day. All animals shall be given rest equal to or greater than their time working on set.

citations.title: Mastering Animal Work on Film Sets: 17 Essential Tips for Success
citations.excerpt: Ensure that appropriate personnel, such as animal handlers and veterinary staff, are present on set. Their expertise is crucial in maintaining a safe environment.

remedy.detail: Engage a professional animal handler for all scenes involving the dog and cat. Develop and implement a comprehensive animal welfare plan, including provisions for adequate rest, exercise, and a safe environment for the animals. Ensure a Certified Animal Safety Representative is present on set to monitor animal action and compliance with industry standards.

flags.finding: The casual depiction of alcohol consumption, specifically Jay's dialogue about 'drinking beers' and getting 'ripped' in S060, may require edits for release in the UAE. While recent reforms have eased some alcohol restrictions, media guidelines still prohibit direct or indirect advertising of alcoholic beverages, and the casual portrayal could be seen as promotional.

citations.title: UAE issues guidelines for sponsored social media posts | The National
citations.excerpt: Advertising for alcoholic beverages or narcotics is not permitted in any form, whether directly or indirectly

remedy.detail: Edit dialogue to remove explicit mentions of getting 'ripped' from alcohol and reduce the casual emphasis on beer consumption, particularly when linked with other illicit activities.

flags.finding: The screenplay includes references to alcohol use, specifically Jay's intention to 'drink some beers, get ripped, and... get laid' in S060. While there is no explicit on-screen consumption of alcohol, the references are casual and associated with irresponsible behavior and illicit drug use. This contributes to the overall mature content but is not a primary driver for an R rating on its own, given that there is generally no limit on alcohol use for R-rated films.

citations.title: R (MPA) | Rating System Wiki | Fandom
citations.excerpt: There is no limit on alcohol, tobacco, prescribed drugs or marijuana use.

citations.title: Ratings Guide - MPA Film Ratings
citations.excerpt: Substance Abuse: Usually indicates an overindulgence/dependency on or addiction to drugs (illegal or prescription) and/or alcohol. It is usually used when both drugs and alcohol are involved. However, sometimes the term is used in lieu of Drug Abuse or Alcohol Abuse. The more graphic the depiction, the higher the rating. [PG-13, R]

remedy.detail: No specific action is required for alcohol use to achieve an R rating. To achieve a lower rating, references to alcohol use in conjunction with illicit drug use or irresponsible behavior would need to be removed or altered.

flags.finding: Scene S009 depicts a knife being used to open a paper bundle. Even for non-aggressive use, a real knife poses a risk of accidental injury.

citations.title: Safety Guide to Using Prop Weapons | School of the Arts Academic Information
citations.excerpt: Treat all prop weapons like real weapons. Handle all prop guns as if loaded. Treat all prop knives as sharp. Be especially conscious of the point on bladed weapons, as they can still cause penetrative injury. Prop weapons can cause severe harm or worse and should be treated with respect.

citations.title: Prop knives for film use? | DVXuser.com
citations.excerpt: For scenes involving stabbing/slashing/running with the knife....you definitely want a rubber/prop one for those scenes. Though for any establishing shots, you will want a "hero" knife that can stand up to extreme close ups. Having a "hero" and a rubber duck is important so you can switch between them for safety, yet keep the authenticity.

remedy.detail: Replace the real knife with a dull prop knife or a retractable stage knife for close-ups and any action where the blade is visible. If a real knife is absolutely necessary for a specific shot (e.g., extreme close-up of cutting), it must be handled by a trained prop master, and strict safety protocols must be in place, including clear safety zones and communication with the performer.

flags.finding: The frequent use of religious exclamations like 'Jesus' and 'God' as casual expletives throughout the screenplay, while not intended as direct blasphemy, could be interpreted as disrespectful or mocking of religious terms in the UAE. Given the strict blasphemy laws and cultural sensitivities, these instances may require editing to avoid offending religious sentiments.

citations.title: United Arab Emirates Legislations | Federal Law by Decree Concerning Combating Discrimination, Hatred and Extremism
citations.excerpt: Blasphemy: Every act that would insult Divine Essence, religions, prophets, messengers, divine books, or Houses of Worship in accordance with the provisions of this Decree by Law. ... Article (4) Insult, defame, slander, mock or curse any of the religions or any of their rituals or sanctities, or disrupting the holding of licensed religious rituals or celebrations or disrupting them with violence or threats.

remedy.detail: Replace religious expletives with non-religious alternatives or remove them where possible. The philosophical discussion about 'theocracy' in Star Wars is less likely to be an issue.
